steps.say: Split-thickness grafts are carrying epidermis with a superficial dermal slice. Thin harvests run from zero point zero zero eight up to zero point zero one two inches. Medium harvests run from zero point zero one two up to zero point zero one eight inches. Thick harvests run from zero point zero one eight up to zero point zero two four inches. Thin slices are taking fastest while thick slices are matching colour best.
steps.tx: **Split-thickness skin grafts (STSG)** are carrying **epidermis** with a superficial variable **dermis** slice. **Thin grafts of 0.008 to 0.012 inches** with **medium grafts of 0.012 to 0.018 inches** and **thick grafts of 0.018 to 0.024 inches** are forming the grades. Thin slices are taking fastest while thick slices are matching colour best.

vis.alt: Split skin graft with epidermis and thin dermis beside full skin graft with whole dermis, and a vascular pedicle flap for contrast.
vis.caption: Split versus full graft thickness with dermis shown. Grades and take phases are in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: Full-thickness grafts are carrying epidermis with the entire dermis and adnexae. Minimal secondary contracture is following the whole-dermis harvest. Well-vascularised beds are demanded for survival. Eyelids with ears and noses are wearing full-thickness grafts best. Whole dermis is resisting contracture but starving without vessels.
steps.tx: **Full-thickness skin grafts (FTSG)** are carrying **epidermis** with the **entire dermis** including **adnexal structures**. Minimal **secondary contracture** is following the whole-dermis harvest. **Well-vascularised beds** are demanded for survival. Eyelids with ears and noses are wearing full-thickness grafts best. Whole dermis is resisting contracture but starving without vessels.

steps.say: Graft take is marching through three sequential phases. Plasmatic imbibition during the first 24 to 48 hours is soaking the graft. Inosculation at 48 to 72 hours is joining the capillaries. Revascularisation is perfusing the graft last. Soak, join, then perfuse.
steps.tx: Graft take is marching through **three sequential phases**. **Plasmatic imbibition** during the first **24 to 48 hours** is soaking the graft. **Inosculation** at **48 to 72 hours** is joining the capillaries. **Revascularisation** is perfusing the graft last. Soak, join, then perfuse.

steps.say: Plasmatic imbibition is feeding grafts by passive capillary sipping. Nutrient and tissue fluid absorption is swelling the graft steadily. A recorded weight gain of 20 to 40 percent is marking the soak. Pink viable beds are weeping the fluid that white avascular beds cannot supply. Grafts are drinking before vessels are joining.
steps.tx: **Plasmatic imbibition** is feeding grafts by passive **capillary absorption** of nutrients and tissue fluid. A recorded **weight gain of 20 to 40 percent** is marking the soak. Pink viable beds are weeping the fluid that white avascular beds cannot supply. Grafts are drinking before vessels are joining.

steps.say: Inosculation is aligning graft with recipient capillaries end to end. Direct micro-anastomosis between donor and bed buds is opening the channels. A timed kiss around day 3 is joining the circuits. Endothelial buds are reaching across the gap from both sides. Blood flow is resuming through joined channels within hours. Aligned capillaries are kissing on day three.
steps.tx: **Inosculation** is aligning **graft donor capillaries** with **recipient bed buds** end to end. Direct **micro-anastomosis** is opening the channels around **day 3**. Endothelial buds are reaching across the gap from both sides. Blood flow is resuming through joined channels within hours. Aligned capillaries are kissing on day three.

steps.say: Primary contraction is snapping grafts smaller at the moment of harvest. Immediate elastic recoil through dermal elastin is powering the snap. Full-thickness grafts with abundant elastin are recoiling hardest. Thick grafts are shrinking most because elastin fills deep dermis. Harvested elastin is springing back at once.
steps.tx: **Primary contraction** is snapping grafts smaller at the moment of harvest. Immediate **elastic recoil** through dermal **elastin** is powering the snap. **Full-thickness grafts** with abundant elastin are recoiling hardest. Thick grafts are shrinking most because elastin fills deep dermis. Harvested elastin is springing back at once.

steps.say: Secondary contraction is dragging grafted wounds smaller weeks later. Wound bed myofibroblast winching after grafting is powering the drag. Thin split-thickness grafts with scant dermis are suffering most. Pressure garments with splints are fighting the myofibroblast winch for months. Myofibroblasts are winching thin grafts hardest.

steps.say: Haematoma beneath grafts is killing takes commonest of all. Blood pooled under the graft is lifting it off its feeding bed. The top single cause of graft failure is collecting blood. Tie-over bolsters with quilting sutures are pressing grafts onto beds to stop collections. Pooled blood is lifting grafts to death.

steps.say: Composite grafts are sandwiching skin upon cartilage or fat. Alar and eyelid defects with cartilage backing are taking the sandwiches. A capped diameter of one point five centimetres is limiting the size. Peripheral bed ingrowth alone is feeding the centres. Sandwich grafts are staying small or centres are dying.
